pitfalls: Do not describe the tool -- describe the decision the tool automated and the error costs you priced.
Do not skip the failure: what the first version got wrong is the most credible part.
points: Name the decision (block? prioritize? route?), the data and labels, the model family and why
Show the economics: how you set the threshold from false-alarm vs miss costs
Show the lifecycle: how you monitored drift and what triggered retraining
Close with measured impact: precision/recall before and after, analyst hours saved
behavioral.prompt: Walk me through a detection you built or improved -- the data, the model, and how you knew it worked.

pitfalls: Do not say 'we tuned it' -- name the specific change: which features, which threshold, which exclusions.
Do not hide the tradeoff: less noise always costs something; name what you paid.
points: Start with the pain: alert volume, precision, and what the noise was costing
Name the diagnosis: which features, thresholds, or scope caused the noise
Describe the tuning as measurement: what you changed, what the FP rate did, what recall did
Close with the operating point you chose and why the tradeoff was right
behavioral.prompt: Tell me about a noisy detection you tamed -- what was firing, and how did you fix it without losing coverage?

pitfalls: Do not recite the technology -- translate it into their risk, their budget, their downtime.
Do not condescend: the executive's questions are sharper than the engineer's, just aimed differently.
points: Set the scene: who they were, what decision they owned, what they feared
Show the translation: the one-sentence business version of the technical control
Name the objection they raised and how you answered it in their language
Close with the decision they made and what happened next
behavioral.prompt: Describe a time you explained a technical security control to a non-technical stakeholder who owned the decision.

sections.heading: ML detection vocabulary
items: Supervised: learns from labels; strong on known, blind to novel
Unsupervised/anomaly: learns normal; catches novel, noisier
Precision = TP/(TP+FP) -- analyst trust; Recall = TP/(TP+FN) -- coverage
Accuracy lies on imbalanced data; judge with precision/recall or PR curves
Thresholds are economic: deploy at minimum expected loss, not 0.50
SHAP: fair division of the prediction among features -- the why behind the score

sections.heading: Adversarial & agentic
items: Evasion (test-time), poisoning/backdoors (train-time), extraction, inversion
Problem-space constraints define real evasion -- functionality must survive
Guardrails in layers: filter input, allowlist tools, filter output, human gate
Agents get least privilege: read tools freely, action tools on approval
Drift monitoring is a security control: investigate the cause before re-baselining

sections.heading: Math formula sheet
items: Bayes: P(M|A) = P(A|M)P(M)/P(A) -- multiply by the base rate
F1 = 2PR/(P+R); AUC 0.5 = coin flip
Entropy H = -sum(p log2 p); 50/50 = 1 bit; gain = parent - weighted children
z = (x-mean)/std; |z|>3 is the conventional alarm line
a.b = sum(a_i b_i); cos = a.b/(|a||b|); (m x n)(n x p) -> (m x p)
GD: w := w - lr*grad; lr too high diverges
Cross-entropy -log(p_true) for classification; MSE for regression
K-means: assign, recompute, repeat; Isolation Forest: short path = anomaly

sections.heading: Assessment day rules
items: 180 minutes; evidence costs 2 minutes per panel -- budget it
Weakest domains get more items: the test hunts your gaps
Labs are scored on checks passed -- read each check's hint
Pass: 75% overall with no domain below 60%

cheatsheet.title: ThreatLocker Assessment Prep -- AI-Aided Cybersecurity & Math Cheatsheet

adaptive_rules.calibration: Phase 1 fixes the baseline: 4 medium items (mins 4-5), one per pillar group. No adaptation until all four are answered.
adaptive_rules.difficulty_proxy: Scenario intensity is proxied by mins (4-5 standard, 6 stretch). After 2 consecutive correct in a domain, prefer stretch items; after 2 wrong, prefer standard.
adaptive_rules.evidence_budget: Each evidence panel costs 2 minutes of the 180 (matches simulation.evidence_cost_mins). Panels are optional; skipping saves time but forfeits context.
adaptive_rules.no_repeats: Each scenario and each lab may appear at most once per sitting.
adaptive_rules.objective_coverage: Within a domain, prefer items whose objectives have not yet been tested this sitting.
adaptive_rules.weakest_domain_targeting: Maintain a running per-domain score (correct/total). After calibration, draw the next scenario from domains scoring below 0.70, weighted by deficit (0.70 - score). Domains at or above 0.70 are drawn only when no weak domain has unseen items left.

lab_pool.selection: Phase 3 draws one lab from each group (detection, defense, role/agentic), preferring labs whose domains are weakest for the candidate.

pass_criteria.details: A candidate who aces scenarios but fails every lab has not demonstrated hands-on skill; a candidate who passes labs but collapses on scenarios has not demonstrated judgment. Both bars are load-bearing.
pass_criteria.lab_bar: At least 70% of lab checks passed across the three labs.

phases.note: Includes exactly one math-foundations drill: quantitative reasoning is tested from the first quarter-hour.
phases.title: Warm-up calibration

phases.adaptive: Full weakest-domain targeting across all 21 AI-aided/role/math domains plus the base pillars (Zero Trust, graphs). Math-foundations stays in the weak-domain pool for the whole phase.
phases.title: Adaptive scenario drill

phases.adaptive: Lab selection adapts: each lab is drawn from the group matching the candidate's weakest pillar so far.
phases.scoring: Each lab scored by checks passed / total checks; hints are free but cost time.
phases.title: Hands-on labs

phases.adaptive: Scenario selection within the track follows weakest-objective targeting.
phases.note: Candidate chooses one role track at the start of the sitting (Detection Engineer, Solutions Engineer, Junior DevOps, Special Projects). 6 items from the chosen track, 2 cross-pillar stretch items.
